goal: Build an insurance claim intake workflow. It should validate the policy number, check whether the reported damage is covered by the policy, collect the missing claim details, forward claims above EUR 5000 or with signs of fraud to a human adjuster, never promise a payout amount, and give the customer a claim reference and the next steps.

design.summary: Intake an insurance claim by validating the policy number, checking coverage for the reported damage, collecting missing claim details, routing high-value or suspicious claims to a human adjuster, and providing the customer with a claim reference and next steps without promising any payout amount.
assumptions: The workflow can access policy, coverage, claim, and customer records through external systems.
A claim reference can be generated by the workflow or an external case system.
Human adjusters are available to receive escalations for high-value or potentially fraudulent claims.
Coverage determination is based on policy terms and reported damage details available at intake time.
successCriteria: Policy number is validated against the policy system.
The reported damage is checked against policy coverage and the result is communicated accurately.
Any missing mandatory claim details are collected before completion or clearly flagged for follow-up.
Claims above EUR 5000 or with signs of fraud are forwarded to a human adjuster.
The workflow never promises a payout amount.
The customer receives a claim reference and clear next steps at the end of the interaction.
constraints: Do not promise, estimate, or imply a payout amount.
Escalate to a human adjuster when claim amount exceeds EUR 5000 or fraud indicators are present.
Only collect data necessary to complete intake and route the claim.
Must preserve a clear audit trail of validation, coverage check, and escalation decisions.

design.coverageRationale: This workflow mixes verification, coverage interpretation, data completion, fraud screening, escalation, and customer communication. A medium-sized test set is sufficient to cover the primary success path plus boundary conditions around missing data, coverage denial, high-value routing, fraud suspicion, and messaging safeguards. Ten cases balances breadth and efficiency while keeping the plan reviewable.

coveragePlan.reason: Verifies the standard end-to-end flow when policy is valid, damage is covered, details are complete, and no escalation is needed.
Confirms the workflow correctly identifies non-covered damage and still provides a reference and next steps without promising payment.
Ensures the workflow rejects or halts on invalid policy records and does not proceed with unsupported intake.
Checks that the workflow identifies and collects incomplete claim information before finalizing intake.
Validates automatic handoff to a human adjuster when the claim amount exceeds the escalation threshold.
Ensures suspected fraud is routed to a human adjuster immediately and not handled solely by automation.
Confirms the workflow can distinguish between a valid policy and an uncovered incident type.
Verifies a unique claim reference is generated and attached to the intake outcome.
Checks that the next-steps message is clear, helpful, and avoids any payout promise or amount estimate.

coveragePlan.category: boundary conditions around EUR 5000 and borderline fraud signals
coveragePlan.reason: Tests decision boundaries at the escalation threshold and ambiguous fraud indicators to prevent routing errors.

agents.name: Intake Route Router
agents.goal: Select exactly one intake branch based on policy validity, coverage status, missing details, escalation threshold, and fraud signals.
agents.backstory: An intake routing specialist that decides the single correct branch and never performs intake work itself.
guardrails: Own no tasks and produce no customer-facing output.
Select exactly one route based only on the available intake conditions.
Never duplicate classification or route evaluation inside a separate task.

agents.name: Claim Intake Specialist
agents.goal: Validate policy, check coverage, collect missing details, assess escalation triggers, generate a claim reference, and prepare customer next steps without implying any payout.
agents.backstory: A careful insurance intake operator who follows minimal-data principles and preserves an audit trail for every intake decision.
guardrails: Do not promise, estimate, or imply any payout amount.
Collect only data necessary to complete intake and route the claim.
Escalate to a human adjuster when claim amount exceeds EUR 5000 or fraud indicators are present.
Preserve a clear audit trail of validation, coverage check, and escalation decisions.
Provide a claim reference and clear next steps in the final customer message.

tasks.name: Valid Intake Route
tasks.description: Handle a claim intake when the policy number is valid and coverage can be assessed. Validate the policy number, check coverage, identify any missing mandatory claim details, assess fraud indicators and amount-based escalation, create a claim reference, and prepare customer next steps. If needed, forward the claim to a human adjuster.
tasks.expectedOutput: A completed intake outcome with validation status, coverage result, missing details if any, escalation decision if applicable, claim reference, and customer next steps.

tasks.name: Invalid Policy Route
tasks.description: Handle cases where the provided policy number is invalid or inactive. Record the validation failure, avoid proceeding with coverage or escalation processing, generate or obtain a claim reference if permitted for intake logging, and provide next steps to the customer.
tasks.expectedOutput: A rejection or stop-processing outcome that clearly states the policy number is invalid, includes a claim reference if available, and gives the customer next steps without discussing payout.

tasks.name: Missing Details Route
tasks.description: Handle cases where mandatory claim details are incomplete. Identify the missing fields, request only the necessary details, preserve the audit trail, and continue to next steps once intake can be completed or clearly flag follow-up.
tasks.expectedOutput: A list of missing mandatory claim details, a request for only necessary follow-up information, and intake next steps.

tasks.name: Escalation Route
tasks.description: Handle claims that exceed EUR 5000 or show fraud indicators. Forward the claim to a human adjuster with the reason and priority, then produce a customer-safe status update and claim reference.
tasks.expectedOutput: An escalation record showing the reason, priority, forwarded status, claim reference, and customer next steps.
